_comment: A fixed mutant set for the polygon, used by scripts/benchmark.py to exercise
the engine without spending API calls. These are hand-written to resemble what
the model produces; they measure the ENGINE (apply, run, verdict), not model
quality. `expected` is the verdict predicted by reading tests/fixtures/
victim_project/WEAK_TESTS.md. A mismatch is a finding either way.

victim/cache.py::LRUCache.get.description: reading a key no longer refreshes its recency, so the hottest keys are the ones evicted
a miss is counted as a hit, so cache hit-rate metrics silently read 100%

victim/cache.py::LRUCache.set.description: the cache evicts one entry early, so it never holds its full capacity
eviction drops the newest entry instead of the oldest, inverting the whole LRU policy

victim/cache.py::LRUCache.invalidate_pre.description: the prefix test is inverted, so bulk invalidation quietly removes nothing
victim/cache.py::LRUCache.invalidate_pre.search_block: doomed = [key for key in self._data if key.startswith(prefix)]
victim/cache.py::LRUCache.invalidate_pre.replace_block: doomed = [key for key in self._data if prefix.startswith(key)]

victim/cache.py::LRUCache.invalidate_pre.description: the count of invalidated keys is never returned, so callers cannot tell whether anything was purged

victim/cache.py::LRUCache.invalidate.description: invalidating an existing key reports failure, so retry loops invalidate forever

victim/cache.py::LRUCache.__init__.description: a capacity of zero is accepted, producing a cache that evicts every write

victim/pagination.py::Page.has_next.description: the last page reports that another page follows, so clients loop one page past the end

victim/pagination.py::Page.has_prev.description: the first page reports a previous page, so back buttons render on page one

victim/pagination.py::page_count.description: page counting truncates instead of rounding up, so the final partial page is unreachable
an empty collection reports one page, so the UI renders an empty page instead of an empty state

victim/pagination.py::paginate.description: every page is offset by one page, so the first page of results is never shown
each page returns one item too few, so one record per page disappears
page zero is accepted and silently returns an empty slice instead of erroring
victim/pagination.py::paginate.search_block:
if page < 1:
        raise ValueError("page must be >= 1")
victim/pagination.py::paginate.replace_block:
if page < 0:
        raise ValueError("page must be >= 1")

victim/parsing.py::parse_duration.description: surrounding whitespace is no longer trimmed, so a value copied from a config file raises
multi-unit durations keep only the last unit, so "1h30m" parses as 30 minutes
a bare number is read as minutes rather than seconds, inflating every timeout sixtyfold

victim/parsing.py::parse_key_values.description: a value containing '=' now raises instead of parsing, breaking query strings and connection URLs
values keep their surrounding whitespace, so "a = 1" yields " 1" and comparisons fail

victim/pricing.py::apply_discount.description: the discount cap acts as a floor, so capped promotions give away more than intended
a negative percentage is accepted and increases the price instead of erroring
prices are rounded to whole units, so every discounted total loses its cents
the discount is computed ten times too large, zeroing out most orders

victim/text.py::truncate.description: truncation cuts one character too many, dropping a letter from every shortened string
a string exactly at the limit is truncated anyway, mangling values that fit

victim/text.py::normalize_whitespace.description: None returns None instead of an empty string, so callers crash on concatenation
words are joined without a separator, collapsing sentences into one run-on token
